GitHubPullRequest.title: fix: Ignore duplicate modifier key releases in keyboard chords
GitHubPullRequest.description:
Fixes #344156

When using Apple Universal Control, VS Code can receive repeated modifier `keyup` events without an intervening corresponding `keydown`. Single-modifier chord handling interprets these as a double tap and cancels the pending chord. For example, `Cmd+K`, release all keys, then `V` can report `(⌘K, ⌘) is not a command` before V is pressed.

This change tracks released modifiers in `AbstractKeybindingService` and ignores subsequent releases of the same modifier until its next keydown. It uses `code` when available to distinguish left and right modifiers, with a fallback to the normalized `keyCode`. A new keydown allows the next release to be processed, preserving intentional modifier double taps.

### Validation

- Common keybinding suites: **72 passing**, including 11 added regression cases covering all four modifiers, pending chords, intentional double taps, left/right identities, Shift/Cmd release ordering, and composition events. Tests were run through targeted transpilation and the existing Node unit test runner.
- Targeted TypeScript check and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Physical Universal Control test: backported this change to an isolated VS Code 1.143.1 test app and tested a NiZ keyboard shared from a Mac mini to a MacBook. Both `Cmd+K V` and `Shift+Cmd+K V` opened the Markdown preview to the side. Troubleshooting logs confirmed duplicate Meta/Shift releases were ignored and `markdown.showPreviewToSide` was invoked.

A full product build and full integration test run have not been performed.

### Manual verification

1. Use Universal Control to share a keyboard from one Mac to another.
2. On the receiving Mac, open a Markdown file and configure the preview keybindings from #344156.
3. Press `Cmd+K`, release all keys, then press `V`. Repeat with `Shift+Cmd+K`, release all keys, then `V`.
4. Verify that both shortcuts open the side preview without a modifier-only invalid-chord message. Repeat using the receiving Mac's built-in keyboard.

GitHubPullRequest.title: Prune non-matching directories from recursive watches on Linux
GitHubPullRequest.description:
Parcel adds an inotify watch for every directory under a recursive watch, while includes are only applied to events afterwards. E.g. watching /usr/lib with the include `python*/site-packages/*.dist-info` added a watch for every directory under /usr/lib, which can exhaust fs.inotify.max_user_watches (ENOSPC).

Derive Parcel ignore patterns from the leading components of the includes: simple components are negated per level (`!(python*)`, `*/!(site-packages)`), complex ones by listing existing non-matching names. Emitted events are unchanged since ignored paths could not match an include. Capped at 100 patterns, since Parcel checks each pattern linearly.

On my system (Ubuntu 26.04), I get [ENOSPC](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/linux#_visual-studio-code-is-unable-to-watch-for-file-changes-in-this-large-workspace-error-enospc) and when looking closer this is unexpectedly caused by each vscode process monitoring the regexp [`python*/site-packages/{*.dist-info,*.dist-info/**}`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/blob/main/src/managers/common/packageWatcher.ts#L73C55-L74C64) in `/usr/lib`, which causes 16k inotify entries per `vscode` window. The regexp used by `vscode-python-environments` looks reasonable, and Parcel's logic makes sense given the provided information, so it seems that the right thing is to fix the glue inbetween. I had to apply a few heuristics but tried to stay simple and conservative.

GitHubPullRequest.title: chat: keep a real pointer from hovering the sticky request bubble test
GitHubPullRequest.description:
Main CI has failed on Linux X64 `Unit Tests (Electron)` since #344806 ([491449](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=491449), [491461](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=491461), [491479](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=491479), 491498), in `ChatListWidget › uses the request bubble as the sticky source and content`:

```
hoverRestoredState: {
+   sourceBackground: 'rgb(4, 5, 6)',   // hover color
-   sourceBackground: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)',
    sourceSynchronized: false,          // .request-bubble-hovered was removed
```

## Cause

After the synthetic `mouseleave`, the test removes the class-driven hover (`sourceSynchronized: false`), but the bubble keeps the hover color. The only other rule that sets it is `.rendered-markdown.clickable:hover` (`chat.css`), so a **real pointer** is over the bubble. #344806 added `electron-browser` focus tests that focus the hidden test window's web contents and add and remove a focused `WebContentsView`. They run earlier in the single-page Electron run. On Linux (Xvfb), the window then takes part in pointer hover, and `:hover` matches whatever sits under the Xvfb pointer. PR CI splits the Electron suite across workers, which is why neither PR's own CI caught it. Root cause is posted on #344806.

## Change (test only)

The test container gets `pointer-events: none`. The test only drives hover with dispatched `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` events, which still fire, so a real pointer can no longer apply `:hover` to the bubbles it checks. The product is unchanged.

## Validation

- **Linux, the run that reproduces it:** def 111 [491516](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=491516) on this branch, as a CI build with Linux only. `Unit Tests (Electron)`, the full single-page run, **passed with 69,453 passing**, including `✔ uses the request bubble as the sticky source and content`. The same job on main fails it every time.
- **Chromium locally:** the test passes.
- eslint is clean.

> Authored with Copilot

GitHubPullRequest.title: Optimize chat window resizing performance
GitHubPullRequest.description:
This pull request addresses performance issues related to resizing the chat window in the agents interface. The changes focus on reducing redundant style recalculations and layout measurements that were identified as the primary cause of slow resizing.

### Key Changes:
- **Terminal Resizing Optimization**: Layout now runs once after terminal reflow, reducing DOM scans from 4 to 1 per resize.
- **Background Replicas Improvement**: Hidden backgrounds no longer measure geometry, eliminating unnecessary reads.
- **Queued Terminal Layouts**: Duplicate frame requests are coalesced, and pending work is canceled upon disposal.

### Testing:
- Added eight regression tests; all 59 targeted tests were executed and passed.
- Full TypeScript and hygiene checks have passed.

These optimizations aim to enhance the user experience by providing smoother resizing without altering any visual or accessibility aspects of the chat interface. Further profiling is recommended to quantify the performance improvements.

GitHubPullRequest.title: chat: Keep Mermaid diagrams mounted while a response streams
GitHubPullRequest.description:
Mermaid diagrams render into a webview `<iframe>` inside a chat output code block. While a response was still streaming, every markdown update re-rendered the whole markdown part and reset its container, which detached and reinserted that iframe. Detaching an iframe destroys its browsing context, so the diagram reloaded on every token and flickered heavily.

Measured on a streaming response containing a diagram:

| | Webview reloads during 14s of streaming |
|---|---|
| Before | **84** |
| After | **0** |

> [!NOTE]
> A side-by-side before/after screen recording is attached in a comment below.

In the "before" state the diagram never even finishes drawing — it reloads faster than Mermaid can render, so it sits on *"Rendering code block…"*. The recording harness initially failed outright with `Frame was detached`, which is the bug itself.

## Approach

Reconcile the rendered markdown in place instead of clearing it, so a reused code block and its matching ancestors stay connected to the document.

- **`markdownRenderer`** — add a reconciling replacement that keeps reused sync code blocks and their ancestor chain in the DOM, falling back to the previous reset when nothing can be preserved.
- **`chatMarkdownContentPart`** — re-render in place and reuse the part across streamed updates so the diagram survives. Read the layout width through a delegate so a resize is picked up by later renders.
- **`chatListRenderer`** — notify reused parts when their row is remounted after virtualization, keep code block registrations in sync as the part re-renders, and stop the progressive renderer from rewinding past a closing fence that was already rendered.

## Testing

- New coverage in `markdownRenderer.test.ts`, `chatMarkdownContentPart.test.ts` and `chatListRenderer.test.ts` for iframe document preservation (top-level, blockquote and list nesting), remount after virtualization, resize during streaming, and rendering a diagram once its fence closes.
- Full chat browser suite (5577) and base markdown suite (173) pass, plus `typecheck-client` and ESLint.
- Verified end to end in a real Code OSS window in both streaming modes, and confirmed the new remount tests fail when the fix is disabled.

## Notes for reviewers

- This reuse path previously sat behind the `chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.enabled` flag. That gate is removed so the fix applies by default, but the non-experimental path only engages for an append-only update to a part that already contains a rendered output code block. **This is the part most worth a close look.**
- Known pre-existing limitations, not addressed here: collapsing a completed response re-parents (and so reloads) a diagram in the collapsed range, and reordering two diagrams reloads them.

GitHubPullRequest.title: sessions: improve web connection information and host recovery
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary

Make host connections in web `/agents` understandable and recoverable, particularly on phones. Disconnecting a host no longer makes it disappear from the picker, and the information button works with touch as well as mouse and keyboard input.

### Connection controls

- Keep the connection indicator passive, with a separate information button that opens Connection Information and exposes the selected host status to assistive technology.
- Put labeled **Disconnect** (prohibited icon) and **Connect** (plug icon) actions beside the existing host summaries, without a duplicate normal-host list. On web, Disconnect keeps the host selectable and pauses automatic connection; explicit Connect resumes it.
- Show previously dismissed hosts in a separate **Hidden Hosts** section with a labeled **Restore** action. Restore clears dismissal and reruns discovery. Failures or hosts not found are reported without claiming that a connection succeeded. Explicit removal remains in host management.
- Use live status for host summaries and controls. Expanded diagnostic details and exports use the captured snapshot, with that distinction stated in the modal.

### Diagnostics presentation

- Group Copy, Download, Refresh, and Close in the header. On web, Refresh combines rediscovery and snapshot capture.
- Describe picker membership as **selectable / not selectable**, independently of connectivity.
- Center the modal in wide layouts and retain the phone bottom sheet. Use workbench scrolling, keyboard focus containment/restoration, and 44px minimum phone host-action targets.
- Keep diagnostic content factual, activity chronological, and client details collapsed. Copy and Download include the complete captured snapshot, including collapsed content.

## Scope and desktop compatibility

The connection-management changes target web `/agents`. Shared native tunnel behavior is preserved: native disconnect/removal retains persistent dismissal, and native reconnect does not acquire the web-specific suppression-clearing behavior. A separate permanent-removal operation prevents recoverable web Disconnect from changing the existing Remove Host flows.

The new diagnostics modal may share presentation and scrolling improvements with the native Agents window. Native diagnostics remain read-only, Refresh captures local state without rediscovery, and accessibility help describes that native behavior. This is not a general native Agents window or regular VS Code redesign. Authentication and CORS work are outside scope.

## Product validation

Tested the actual local `/agents` build using standalone Chromium on the development machine, with desktop and iPhone device emulation:

- Reproduced the top information button's touch-only failure before fixing it: mouse click and keyboard activation worked, but a touch tap did nothing. After the fix, Playwright touch taps, mouse clicks, Enter, and Space opened diagnostics; the adjacent host picker also remained touch-operable.
- Exercised Connect/Disconnect beside collapsed host summaries, live status updates, replacement-action focus, and existing host removal followed by Hidden Hosts recovery.
- Checked desktop centering, phone action-target height, wheel scrolling, narrow desktop layout, and phone portrait/landscape adaptation. Captured empty/failed discovery and multiple-host scenarios as well.

Phone results are Chromium device emulation, not verification on a physical phone or installed PWA. Real-tunnel network-failure behavior and the full incompatible-host scenario have not been validated end to end.

GitHubPullRequest.title: chat: surface out-of-band subagent approvals
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary

Make pending subagent approvals discoverable independently of where their original launch response is rendered, while preserving the existing confirmation UI.

- Discover pending tool invocations from the chat view model instead of relying on a mounted transcript row to populate the input confirmation carousel.
- Surface approvals from earlier responses in the Sessions list, preserving current-request precedence and the original tool callback. Single-choice file approvals are supported; multi-choice file operations remain in the full chat UI.
- Keep the original subagent pill's pending/active approval highlight and the usual confirmation card with Allow/Skip. Do not add an "action needs your approval" heading, duplicate launch pill, or generic out-of-band shimmer. Ordinary current-request confirmation presentation is preserved.
- Route Accept/Skip commands to the selected carousel item, preserve each item's rendering context, and clean up stale entries when models change.
- Restore edited terminal commands, including extracted directory prefixes, when recreating an approval after switching chats. Observe request-edit entry/exit directly so a pending approval appears immediately when editing ends.

## Investigation findings

The apparent hangs included several distinct cases:

1. **Offscreen approval — addressed here.** A retained subagent continued publishing into its original parent response. The pending invocation and confirmation callback existed in the frontend model, but that historical response was outside the virtualized viewport. Revealing it exposed the existing Allow button. Carousel discovery depended on rendering that row, and the Sessions-list approval model only inspected the latest response. The session-level `inputNeeded` watcher handles owned client-tool execution, not independent rendering of SDK-native shell/file approvals.
2. **Reported failure after Allow — not established by the original export.** That capture ended with two independent approvals pending and did not contain the reported final Allow action. This patch tests correct callback/selection behavior but does not claim to resolve every provider-side post-approval stall.
3. **Large subagent fan-out — not addressed here.** A later capture contained 40 attempted launches: 32 succeeded and eight were rejected by that runtime's 32-concurrent-agent limit. All 32 eventually published child-start events. Earlier `Resource not found` subscriptions preceded delayed child startup; the remaining 18 requested reviews were not hidden running agents.
4. **Foreground completion while a background shell remains alive — not addressed here.** A separate capture showed successful `task_complete`, completed tool calls, and delivered final Markdown, but no protocol `chat/turnComplete` while an attached preview server remained running. That completion-boundary issue is tracked separately in #336083.

Related rendering work: #335899. This PR does not change SDK/CLI versions, runtime concurrency limits, child-start timing, or foreground completion semantics.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` — passed, zero errors.
- Full hygiene for all 14 changed files — passed; pre-commit hygiene also passed.
- Focused Electron suites for `AgentSessionApprovalModel`, `ChatListRenderer`, `ChatSubagentContentPart`, and Sessions-list chat rows — **263 passing, 1 existing pending**.
- Regressions cover completed historical responses, independent Sessions-list Allow buttons, retained-pill highlighting, no extra heading/shimmer, model removal/rebinding, command edits across chat switches, and cancelling request editing without further progress.
- Real browser interaction with the actual chat list, input, terminal editors, and confirmation controls in Dark/Light themes. The original launch stayed unmounted while both approvals appeared; revealing it showed both pills highlighted. Allow cleared only the selected approval/highlight, then the remaining mock approval completed independently. No real shell commands or LLM calls were executed by the mock approvals. Preview processes were stopped after testing.

## Manual validation

Open the existing Component Explorer Server task and select `chat/agent-lifecycle/chatAgentLifecycle/OffscreenSubagentApprovals` (Dark or Light):

1. The conversation starts on a later request with the original launch offscreen.
2. Select **Request Offscreen Approvals**. Both approvals should be available above the input with the existing card style, without an extra count heading or shimmer.
3. Select **Show Original Agent**. Both retained pills should indicate pending approval; the active approval retains its existing emphasis.
4. Select **Allow**, or use **Accept Selected** / **Skip Selected**. Only that invocation should resolve; the other remains pending.
5. Approve the remaining mock check. Its continuation is recorded and the carousel clears.

The fixture's shortcut shim dispatches the real Accept/Skip commands; it is not an end-to-end test of the production keybinding resolver. Sessions-list Allow routing is exercised separately with real row controls in the focused tests.

GitHubPullRequest.title: agentHost: stabilize trusted Codex workspace hooks
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary

- recheck Codex workspace hook trust after provisional thread startup, when a cold app-server has populated its hook catalog
- carry newly discovered trust directly into a lossless pre-turn replacement thread
- repeat a cold resume when hooks become visible only after the initial resume
- distinguish hook discovery failures from an empty catalog so failures do not trigger unnecessary restarts
- wait for the integration test Workspace Trust update before creating its session

## Motivation

A cold Codex process can return an empty `hooks/list` result before its first thread starts. The thread then starts without `hooks.state`, so a trusted workspace `SessionStart` hook does not run for the first turn. This is a product race that surfaced as a flaky timeout in Azure build 473928.

The separate quarantine PR is #336297. This change fixes the underlying product behavior and keeps the trusted integration case active.

## Validation

- hygiene on all three changed files
- 17 focused workspace-hook-trust unit tests
- full Codex customizations integration suite: 6 passing
- trusted/untrusted integration pair repeated in five cold processes: 5/5 passing

## Review

Reviewed with Claude Opus. The review findings around inherited hooks, replacement connections, cold resume, discovery failure signaling, polling overhead, and send-path coverage were addressed before opening this draft.

GitHubPullRequest.title: sessions: Prepare sandbox repositories before session creation
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary

Prepare the selected repository on a capable sandbox host before creating the session, rather than assuming that connecting also supplies a ready checkout.

- Reuse ready or in-progress checkouts, or request a shallow host-side clone and show progress until it is ready.
- Keep host-specific operations behind the advertised capability and a typed, connection-owned project adapter. Preserve older pre-cloned hosts and existing sessions.
- Pass the resolved host directory into session creation and rebind workspace-scoped customizations when the directory changes.
- Surface failures and cancellation, allow an explicit user retry after a failed clone, and apply a three-minute deadline to both acknowledgement and readiness.
- Add regression coverage and document the client-side lifecycle. No token-provisioning changes are included.

## Protocol boundary

The shared `IAgentConnection` interface does not expose arbitrary RPC dispatch. The concrete transport client retains the low-level host-extension sender, while `CloudSandboxProjectsClient` exposes typed project operations and validates the capability, catalogue entries, and clone response. The resolver no longer names wire methods or handles untyped RPC responses.

The sandbox connection factory owns each adapter by connection identity. Teardown cancels preparation and removes only that connection's adapter, leaving a replacement at the same address intact. No standard AHP schema, command-map, protocol-version, or clone wire-payload changes are introduced.

## Validation

- 135 focused unit tests passed, covering adapter validation and lifetime, repository preparation, sandbox provisioning and credentials, transport requests, and customization scopes.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Repository hygiene passed for the staged files, including during the commit hook.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` and `git diff --check` passed.

## Manual verification still needed

- [ ] Start a sandbox session whose repository has not been cloned; verify progress and that the first turn runs in the returned checkout.
- [ ] Confirm a ready checkout is reused and existing sessions retain their directories.
- [ ] Cancel preparation and retry a failed clone; verify that no turn starts before preparation succeeds.
- [ ] Verify workspace-scoped MCP configuration follows the prepared checkout.

Full-build and live-sandbox/end-to-end verification have not been run.

GitHubPullRequest.title: sessions: Support Dev Containers on SSH and Tunnel hosts
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary

Allow Agents Window sessions to run in Dev Containers on SSH and Tunnel hosts, using the same workspace-mode picker and session handoff as local Dev Containers.

- Run the bundled Dev Container CLI on the source host and carry the container Agent Host protocol through the existing SSH/Tunnel connection using capability-gated extension RPCs.
- Share draft/session preparation, trust checks, configuration/model/agent carryover, worktree lifecycle, rollback, and reconnect behavior between local and remote source providers.
- Preserve source-host identity in persisted container providers and Open in VS Code routing. Keep old hosts and unsupported/nested sources from offering container execution.
- Add SSH ProxyCommand support, standard initial `none` authentication, and known-hosts path handling needed for Docker Sandbox SSH connections.
- Include the generated connection token in standalone dev-host startup URLs so SSH command overrides work without disabling authentication; persistent log URLs remain token-free.
- Add actual Agents Window UI smoke tests for SSH and opt-in real private Tunnels, with isolated hosts/authentication and mock model traffic. Fix raw SSH identity classification and nested workspace submenus exposed by these tests.
- Address both review findings: await provider-started source connections and keep stale failures from disconnecting a replacement attempt.

Uses the existing `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled` setting. Remote source hosts must run a version advertising the new Dev Container capability. The remote server package now includes `@devcontainers/cli`.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, scoped hygiene/ESLint, and diff whitespace checks — passed.
- Affected protocol/provider/picker suites — 811 passing, 11 pending; SSH compatibility suites — 176 passing.
- Follow-up widget/configuration/picker regressions — 223 passing; connection readiness/ownership suites — 29 passing.
- Smoke/automation compilation and hygiene — passed.
- **Actual UI smoke run:** local, SSH, and Tunnel Dev Container suites passed together (3 tests). Each remote case has consecutive successful local UI runs. Tests drive host connection, remote folder selection, Use Dev Container, prompt submission, the rendered response, and session reopening, and verify the outer transport and nested container routing.
- Separate live backend tests also verified Docker Sandbox SSH bootstrap and container session recovery after reconnect over localhost SSH and the real Dev Tunnels relay.
- Test tunnels, containers, processes, and temporary credentials were cleaned up; captured smoke logs were checked for real account-token leakage.

## Smoke test prerequisites

The new remote UI smoke cases live in `test/smoke/src/areas/agentsWindow/agentsWindow.test.ts`; instructions are in `test/smoke/README.md`.

- SSH uses a self-contained loopback SSH fixture and runs with Docker on Linux CI and supported local macOS/Linux machines.
- The real Tunnel case is opt-in via `VSCODE_SMOKE_TEST_TUNNEL_TOKEN`, with a compatible CLI and existing/explicit license consent. It does not require or consume account credentials in ordinary PR smoke jobs.
- Source-mode Tunnel tests use an isolated source-app snapshot to supply the missing Code OSS tunnel-authentication metadata; they do not modify shared product files. Packaged runs require the supplied build's tunnel configuration.
- Both use mock model responses, not paid model requests.

The new UI cases have been exercised locally on macOS. Linux CI also ran and passed the SSH Dev Container UI smoke test; the real Tunnel case was skipped as intended without opt-in credentials. All 33 substantive CI checks passed on `2d68a777eeb`. This PR remains a draft and requires one collaborator approval.

GitHubPullRequest.title: fix: memory leak in dialog main service
GitHubPullRequest.description: ### Details Each window that shows a native dialog gets its own queue in `DialogMainService`. The queue is not removed after the dialog finishes and the window closes, so one queue remains for every window that has shown a dialog. ### Change Remove a per-window dialog queue when all of its work has finished. Dialogs that overlap for the same window still share the queue and run in order. ### Before After 37 measured cycles of opening a window, invoking About, and closing the window, `named-function-count3` reports 37 additional `Queue` allocations. Heap retaining paths lead through `DialogMainService.windowDialogQueues`. The outlined `Queue` row identifies the growth removed by this change. Both revisions use the same main-process scenario and a growth threshold of 37. The usual `async.ts` and `event.ts` exclusions are disabled so queue and emitter allocations are visible. Black bars show the initial count, red bars show growth, and labels show the final count. ### After With the same 37 measured cycles, `Queue` growth is 0. The raw heaps contain 2 `Queue` instances before and after, belonging to configuration editing and the no-window dialog queue. No queues remain retained through `windowDialogQueues`. Other event and storage allocations still grow and remain visible below. ### Test Video [test-video.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/633826c1-f8f2-4a60-baa9-b45d1e2d88b2)

GitHubPullRequest.title: sessions: Filter cloud history and surface linked issues
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary

Reduce stale cloud-session history and show which GitHub issues a cloud session is addressing.

- Add `github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.sessionVisibility`, defaulting to `30days`, with `24hours`, `7days`, `30days`, `90days`, and `all` options. There is no `none` option.
- Filter in the Copilot cloud provider using the Task API's most recent activity timestamp, before resolving pull requests or fetching changed files. Refresh on setting changes and cache expiry, and prevent obsolete requests from replacing fresh results.
- Fetch GitHub's structured PR-closing issue relationships and expose them as session artifacts and references for the existing GitHub issue pill. Deduplicate links and update or remove them atomically as metadata changes.

## Behavior and scope

Hiding sessions does not delete or archive them. `all` removes only the age limit; existing session and pull-request exclusions remain unchanged.

Issue detection uses verified GitHub relationships, not incidental PR-body mentions. Cross-repository public GitHub issues are supported; enterprise-hosted issues remain openable artifacts without public GitHub polling. Both PR lookup paths request up to 100 linked issues.

Verified example relationship: PR #336399 links issue #335868.

- Copilot build: `npm run compile-copilot`
- Copilot extension TypeScript check

GitHubPullRequest.title: terminal: show agent host terminals like local terminals
GitHubPullRequest.description:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Terminals that the Agents window opens on an agent host showed a fixed "Agent Host Terminal" tab with the remote icon, whatever ran in them. This titles them by their process, with the usual terminal icons, like local terminals. A terminal on a remote agent host names that host in its description, such as `zsh - devbox`, the way a remote window marks a local terminal with "Local".

## Before / after


<!-- Drop the before/after video here -->



## What changes

- **Title:** agent host terminals are titled by their process, such as `zsh`, then `node` while it runs, as local terminals are. `AgentHostTerminalService` named every terminal "Agent Host Terminal", or "Agent Host (<host>)" when it was opened from an agent host profile, and a fixed name makes a terminal's title static, so the process titles the host reports were ignored.
- **Icon:** the default terminal icon instead of the remote icon. Terminals revived to show a chat tool's command get the chat-sparkle icon, like the agent's local terminals.
- **Remote hosts:** the desktop Agents window shows sessions from every host together, so a terminal on a remote agent host names its host in the description after the title, as in `zsh - devbox`. A remote window marks the exception the same way, showing "Local" through `${local}`. This adds `IShellLaunchConfig.hostLabel` and a `${host}` variable for `terminal.integrated.tabs.title` and `terminal.integrated.tabs.description`, and adds `${host}` to the description's default. Each agent host entry gives the label for its terminals; remote hosts set it to their name, and This Computer leaves it unset.
- **Named terminals:** a caller that passes a name still gets a fixed title, so the Agents window's task runner keeps naming its terminals "Task: <label>", like tasks.
- **Starting and reconnecting:** `AgentHostPty` now reports the host's title when a terminal starts or reconnects. It stored the title without reporting it, so the tab stayed empty until the title next changed.
- **Windows hosts:** a Windows agent host reports the shell's path as the title and never a process name, and the terminal shortens paths only for processes it knows run on Windows, which a custom pty cannot tell it. `AgentHostPty` now reduces `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe` to `pwsh`; without that, the tab would show `C:\Program`.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Terminal owners:** the `terminal.integrated.tabs.description` default changes for everyone. Other terminals have no host label, so they look the same, but this is shared terminal code. Users who customized the setting see the host only if they add `${host}`, as with `${local}` today.
- **Web:** the host label is desktop only. On the web, the Agents window shows one host at a time, so the label would repeat on every terminal.
- **Screen readers:** the host is not announced, because a terminal tab's screen reader label has its title but not its description, as with "Local" today. Changing that changes the label of every terminal, so it belongs in a separate change with an accessibility review.
- **Profiles:** the New Terminal dropdown still lists the agent host profiles as "Agent Host (This Computer)" and "Agent Host (<host>)", which is how you pick a host. Only the terminals created from them change.
- **Before the host replies:** the client does not know the host's shell up front, so the tab title is empty until the host reports it, one round trip after the terminal is created.
- **The video** was recorded from a temporary component fixture that renders the real `AgentHostTerminalService`, `AgentHostPty`, `TerminalInstance` and panel terminal tab against scripted agent hosts, which send what a VS Code agent host sends. "Before" runs the code from `main`, with the same fixture and script.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a session on This Computer and show the Terminal panel: the terminal tab shows the shell's name, such as `zsh`, with the terminal icon and no host.
2. Run `node` in the terminal: the tab shows `node`. Exit it: the tab shows `zsh` again.
3. Open a session on a remote agent host: its terminal shows the host after the title, as in `zsh - devbox`. Select New Terminal (+): the new terminal is titled the same way, not "Agent Host (<host>)".
4. Disconnect the remote host and open its session again: the session's terminal falls back to a local one, which shows no host.
5. Ask the agent to run a command in a terminal, then select Show Terminal on it: the terminal has the chat-sparkle icon and the shell's name, and the host if it is remote.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalInstance.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/agentHostTerminalService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/agentHostPty.test.ts`: 165 passing, 2 pending, including new regression tests that fail without these changes
- `npm run eslint -- $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.ts')`: passed, for the 9 changed files
- Pre-commit hygiene: passed
- A temporary, uncommitted test with a real `TerminalInstance`: the old configuration renders "Agent Host Terminal" with the remote icon; the new one renders `zsh` with the terminal icon, `pwsh` for the Windows path above, and `zsh` for `/bin/zsh`.

There is no tracking issue; this comes from a report of the "Agent Host Terminal" tab in the Agents window.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

GitHubPullRequest.title: Bump actions/github-script from 8.0.0 to 9.0.0
GitHubPullRequest.description:
Bumps [actions/github-script](https://github.com/actions/github-script) from 8.0.0 to 9.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

What's Changed

  • Add ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID to user-agent string by @​Copilot in actions/github-script#695
  • ci: use deployment: false for integration test environments by @​salmanmkc in actions/github-script#712

GitHubPullRequest.title: Clarify Basic SKU protocol requirements for macOS VPN
GitHubPullRequest.description:
## Summary
Clarifies the Basic SKU protocol requirements in the macOS "Native VPN client" section.

## Why
The original note excluded all Basic SKU gateways, but existing Basic SKU gateways may still use SSTP while new Basic SKU gateways can use IKEv2. The macOS native VPN client supports certificate-authenticated IKEv2 connections, but it doesn't support Basic SKU gateways that still use SSTP.

## Reference
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/ikev2-openvpn-from-sstp

## Description

Generates Az.RedisEnterpriseCache 3.0.0 from the stable `2026-09-01` Redis Enterprise API specification.

This update:
- adds migration validation, start/get/undo, and migrated-endpoint unlink commands
- adds maintenance-window and keyspace-notification support
- updates access-policy assignment and database command shapes for the GA API
- intentionally excludes the AccessString surface from this release
- preserves the friendly Start migration command through a custom wrapper over the generated JSON implementation
- removes stale Enterprise capacity when converting a cache to a Gen2 SKU
- refreshes examples, markdown/MAML help, scenario tests, and live recordings

### What
Add new `Az.Resiliency` PowerShell module for `Microsoft.AzureResilienceManagement` — initial GA release based on stable api-version `2026-10-01`.

### Module surface
65 cmdlets, 387 parameter sets:

| Verb | Count | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Get | 16 | `Get-AzResiliencyDrill`, `Get-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlan`, `Get-AzResiliencyUsagePlan` |
| Invoke | 9 | `Invoke-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlanFailover`, `Invoke-AzResiliencyDrillRunFailover` |
| Test | 8 | `Test-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlanReadiness`, `Test-AzResiliencyDrillExecutionValidation` |
| Update | 8 | `Update-AzResiliencyDrill`, `Update-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlan` |
| New | 6 | `New-AzResiliencyDrill`, `New-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlan`, `New-AzResiliencyUsagePlan` |
| Remove | 5 | `Remove-AzResiliencyDrill`, `Remove-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlan` |
| Set | 4 | `Set-AzResiliencyEnrollment`, `Set-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlan` |
| Other | 9 | `Start-`, `Stop-`, `Resume-`, `Sync-`, `Add-`, `Complete-` |

### Swagger diff (2026-09-30-preview → 2026-10-01)
No breaking changes — identical API surface, clean GA promotion.

### AutoRest directives
- **errorDetails type collision** (CS0738/CS0535): deleted read-only `DrillProperties.errorDetails` property
- **Multi-type Body parameter**: renamed 27 action-style POST operationIds to distinct cmdlets
- **Duplicate Invoke prefix**: stripped via subject rename directive
- **RecoveryJobs_Retry**: reordered subject for consistency
- **UsagePlan List1 variant**: renamed to `ListByResourceGroup`

### Generated with
- AutoRest CLI 3.8.0
- @autorest/powershell 4.0.758
- @autorest/modelerfour 4.26.2
- Spec commit: `abfe7853f1382c8124b23be81984196102fd9343`

### Validation
- [x] Build succeeded (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- [x] 65 cmdlets / 387 parameter sets verified
- [x] `generate-info.json` staged
- [x] No forbidden paths (`generated/`, `bin/`, `obj/`) in commit
- [ ] Recorded tests (requires live subscription)

---
Created by Azure SRE Agent: [Open thread](https://sre.azure.com/agents/subscriptions/5417152a-174b-4748-876a-b4e6628d9eb7/resourceGroups/azure-automation-sre-agent/providers/Microsoft.App/agents/azure-automation-agent/views/thread/9c5e5ff1-dd08-4b0f-929a-d215402a19a5)

### Workarounds pending spec fixes (2026-10-01)
- `planType` is returned by the service but marked create-only in the spec (`@visibility(Lifecycle.Create)` → `x-ms-mutability: ["create"]`).
  - CLI: `custom.py` / `commands.py` add it back to `recovery-plan create/show/list/update` output.
  - PowerShell: a README directive marks it readable, which also fixes `Update-AzResiliencyRecoveryPlan` (GET + PUT previously omitted the required `planType`).
- Goal assignments declare `final-state-via: location`, but the initial response may not carry `Location`. PowerShell: a README directive switches create/update to `original-uri` (same approach as `Cdn` / `FrontDoor`); this also avoids the PATCH final result coming back as a JSON string.

These will be removed once the Resiliency spec is updated and the clients are regenerated.

## Description

Enable Change Safety for **12 Azure PowerShell modules across 13 AutoRest submodules**:

- Az.Aks
- Az.CloudService
- Az.Compute
- Az.Dns
- Az.DnsResolver
- Az.EdgeAction
- Az.Fleet
- Az.KeyVault
- Az.RedisEnterpriseCache
- Az.Resources (Authorization.Autorest and DataBoundary.Autorest)
- Az.Storage
- Az.Websites

The PR adds `enable-change-safety: true`, refreshes source-side generation identifiers, and adds Upcoming Release changelog entries. It changes source configuration, custom wrappers, focused tests and documentation, and includes genuinely regenerated HTTP recordings. Repository-root generated archives are unchanged relative to the PR base; archive-bot owns regenerated archive updates.

### Custom wrapper forwarding

- Custom write wrappers discover dynamic Change Safety parameters from their generated write targets and preserve caller-bound values, including an explicitly false `AcquirePolicyToken` switch.
- The CloudService VIP-swap wrapper uses its actual `Az.Accounts\Invoke-AzRestMethod` target instead of a generated private write cmdlet. It forwards bound dynamic parameters only to the POST, not preliminary GETs or polling, and does not expose them when the REST implementation lacks dynamic-parameter support.
- KeyVault region wrappers build separate metadata-filtered dictionaries for preliminary and result reads while retaining Change Safety values for the update.
- Compute and EdgeAction use shared metadata-driven helpers. EdgeAction explicitly copies bound dynamic values into its reconstructed deployment dictionary.
- Storage migration maps all four custom parameter sets to their corresponding generated write variants.
- Websites forwards Change Safety for its only supported public parameter set, `CreateExpanded`. The unsupported identity and JSON parameter sets were removed by #30235, which is already included in this branch.

The read-filtering and reconstructed-dictionary forwarding patterns were checked against #30211. The KeyVault read helper and EdgeAction forwarding helper match that PR's fixed implementations apart from module naming.

Originally merged `main` through #30286 (`4b50751a269`) to resolve the KeyVault blocker. The latest-main merge documented below now advances KeyVault to upstream API `2026-05-15`, preserves all five corresponding upstream recordings without modification, and assigns a fresh generation marker for the combined API upgrade and Change Safety configuration.

Merged upstream main through `3c18cdad234` in merge commit `8fc3931b28e`. Resolved Compute, EdgeAction, and Resources changelog conflicts by preserving both changes. EdgeAction now uses upstream's stable `2026-10-01` API and refreshed recordings while retaining Change Safety opt-in and custom forwarding. Assigned a fresh EdgeAction generation marker for the combined configuration; at that merge, the EdgeAction recordings matched upstream (the later live-recording follow-up below supersedes those recordings).

## Description

<!-- Please add a brief description of the changes made in this PR. If you have an ongoing or finished cmdlet design, please paste the link below. -->

Validate registry names before data-plane requests and pass Docker login credentials as data instead of interpolating PowerShell source.

- Enforce the documented 5–50 ASCII alphanumeric naming rules in cmdlet parameters and the shared data-plane client.
- Use culture-invariant lowercasing when constructing registry endpoints.
- Invoke Docker with structured arguments and pass the password through standard input, preserving the existing output type and error, verbose and warning forwarding.

## Description

<!-- Please add a brief description of the changes made in this PR. If you have an ongoing or finished cmdlet design, please paste the link below. -->

Prepare Az.Cdn for the next major release:

- Use stable API `2026-10-01` for Classic CDN and Azure Front Door.
- Remove AFD URL signing support that was unintentionally included in the stable module despite being a preview feature. Support will remain available in the preview module. Alex Wang confirmed that this removal is not a breaking change.
- Remove standalone EdgeAction management cmdlets, while retaining EdgeAction delivery-rule associations. This removal was pre-announced in [PR #30160](https://github.com/Azure/azure-powershell/pull/30160/changes). All of these cmdlets are supported in the Az.EdgeAction module.
- Regenerate cmdlets and help, and update Classic CDN retirement tests and recordings.

Validation: module builds passed; 61 unit tests and 147 playback test cases passed (148 skipped). Full CI static analysis remains unverified because a local NuGet TLS failure blocked building the analysis tools.

## Description

The Batch service retired the pool usage metrics API and task authentication tokens on 30 September 2024 ([Azure Batch retirements](https://github.com/Azure/Batch/issues/140)). The Batch API has also deprecated the `RetainedData` value of the compute node deallocation, reboot and reimage options ("Deprecated, we encourage you to upload task data to Azure Storage in your task and use `TaskCompletion` instead", [models.tsp](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/main/specification/batch/data-plane/Batch/models.tsp)), and the upcoming 2026-10-01 API version removes it ([Azure/azure-rest-api-specs#44527](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/44527)). Az.Batch still exposes all three. This PR adds the breaking-change attributes so they can be removed in the next major release:

| Cmdlet | Attribute | What is announced |
|---|---|---|
| `Get-AzBatchPoolUsageMetric` | `CmdletDeprecationWithVersion` | The cmdlet is deprecated without a replacement |
| `New-AzBatchTask` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-AuthenticationTokenSettings` | The parameter is deprecated without a replacement |
| `New-AzBatchTask` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-Tasks` | `AuthenticationTokenSettings` property of `PSCloudTask` (input) |
| `New-AzBatchJob` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-JobManagerTask` | `AuthenticationTokenSettings` property of `PSJobManagerTask` (input) |
| `New-AzBatchJobSchedule` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-JobSpecification` | `AuthenticationTokenSettings` property of `PSJobManagerTask` under `JobSpecification` (input) |
| `Get-AzBatchTask` | `CmdletOutputBreakingChangeWithVersion(typeof(PSCloudTask))` | `AuthenticationTokenSettings` property of the output |
| `Get-AzBatchJob` | `GenericBreakingChangeWithVersion` | `AuthenticationTokenSettings` property of `PSJobManagerTask` under the returned `PSCloudJob` |
| `Get-AzBatchJobSchedule` | `GenericBreakingChangeWithVersion` | `AuthenticationTokenSettings` property of `PSJobManagerTask` under the returned `PSCloudJobSchedule` |
| `Start-AzBatchPoolResize` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-ComputeNodeDeallocationOption` | The `RetainedData` value is being removed |
| `Remove-AzBatchComputeNode` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-DeallocationOption` | The `RetainedData` value is being removed |
| `Restart-AzBatchComputeNode` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-RebootOption` | The `RetainedData` value is being removed |
| `Reset-AzBatchComputeNode` | `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion` on `-ReimageOption` | The `RetainedData` value is being removed |

ChangeLog: `* Preannounced breaking changes. Please refer to https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2333229` under `## Upcoming Release`.

Target release: December 2026 (2026-12-01), so the notices ship at least two releases before the spring 2027 major release.

Notes:

- Every attribute says why (the service retirement, or for `RetainedData` the API deprecation), in `ChangeDescription` as a named property, or in the message for the two generic attributes, so the text also shows on the upcoming breaking changes page.
- For the input parameters I used `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersion`, so the warning only shows when that parameter is used. `GenericBreakingChangeWithVersion` on a parameter shows the warning on every call of the cmdlet.
- The breaking-change attributes only check whether a parameter is used, not its value, so the four `RetainedData` warnings show whenever the parameter is used, with any value. Their text names `RetainedData` and says that `Requeue`, `Terminate` and `TaskCompletion` stay. These four parameters are the only ones in Az.Batch that accept `RetainedData`.
- No cmdlet sends `authenticationTokenSettings` unless the user sets it (checked for `New-AzBatchTask`, `New-AzBatchTask -Tasks` and `New-AzBatchJob -JobManagerTask`).

**Questions for the Azure PowerShell team:**

1. Which Az / Az.Batch versions should the attributes use for the spring 2027 major release? I used Az 18.0.0 / Az.Batch 5.0.0 (the next major after Az 17.0.0 in November 2026); please correct them if needed.
2. Optional: `Get-AzBatchPoolUsageMetric` calls an API that the Batch service retired on 30 September 2024. Could a cmdlet like this be removed in a regular (minor) release, or should it wait for the major release like the rest? Either is fine for us.
3. Optional: would you prefer the `RetainedData` warning to show only when `RetainedData` is used? A small subclass of `CmdletParameterBreakingChangeWithVersionAttribute` that overrides `IsApplicableToInvocation` would do it, as Az.Accounts did for `Get-AzAccessToken` in #26929. I tried it locally: the upcoming breaking changes entries stay the same, and the warning shows only with `RetainedData`. Either is fine for us.

## Az.Batch

### `Get-AzBatchJob`

- Cmdlet breaking-change will happen to all parameter sets
  - The Batch service retired task authentication tokens on 30 September 2024, so the AuthenticationTokenSettings property of PSJobManagerTask (in the JobManagerTask property of the returned PSCloudJob) is being deprecated.
  - This change is expected to take effect from Az.Batch version: 5.0.0 and Az version: 18.0.0

Az.StackHCI 3.0.0 applies generated Azure login verification to every exported proxy, including cmdlets that perform only node-local operations.

This change:

- Allows exactly 12 node-local Remote Support, attestation, virtual machine attestation, and logging cmdlets to run without an Az context.
- Retains login verification for the other 39 Azure Resource Manager (ARM)-backed cmdlets.
- Avoids a nested localhost session in Remote Support checks.
- Avoids a localhost session when `Disable-AzStackHCIAttestation` runs locally while preserving explicit management-node targeting.
- Adds regression coverage for the generated proxy split and remoting behavior.

The source generation configuration is updated in this PR. Generated files will be handled separately by the repository's archive workflow. There are no cmdlet API or help changes.

## Description

`tools/BatchModelGenerator` generates the model classes in `src/Batch/Batch/Models.Generated` (the `PS*` classes that wrap the Batch .NET SDK objects returned by the cmdlets). In the Az.Batch 4.0.0 breaking change release (#28767), the certificate models and some pool and node properties were deleted from `Models.Generated` by hand, but the generator wasn't told to skip them. So running the generator on the current SDK (`Microsoft.Azure.Batch` 16.3.1) and following its README brings them back:

- 3 models: `PSCertificate`, `PSCertificateReference`, `PSDeleteCertificateError`
- 8 properties: `CertificateReferences`, `CurrentNodeCommunicationMode`, `ResourceTags` and `TargetNodeCommunicationMode` on `PSCloudPool`; `CertificateReferences`, `ResourceTags` and `TargetNodeCommunicationMode` on `PSPoolSpecification`; `CertificateReferences` on `PSComputeNode`

This PR:

- adds the 3 models to a new skip list (`OmittedTypes`) and the 8 properties to the existing one (`OmittedProperties`) in `Program.cs`. It also drops the `Certificate` entry from `OmittedProperties`, which isn't used once that model is skipped.
- updates the README: the dll path must be absolute (the tool loads it with `Assembly.LoadFile`); the tool targets .NET 5, so on a machine without the .NET 5 runtime it runs with `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor`; where the output goes; to remove a model or property, add it to the skip lists instead of editing the generated files; how to compare the output with the checked-in files.

No change to the module: `Models.Generated` and the cmdlets stay the same, so there is no ChangeLog entry.

### Testing

Ran the generator on `Microsoft.Azure.Batch.dll` 16.3.1 (the version Az.Batch uses), as the README describes, on the .NET 10 runtime:

- Before: 127 files, compared with 124 in `Models.Generated`: the 3 models and 8 properties above come back.
- After: 124 files with the same names, and `git diff --no-index -I "Runtime Version:" -- src/Batch/Batch/Models.Generated <GeneratedFiles>` shows no difference. Each file differs only in the header line that records the .NET runtime used to generate it (`Runtime Version:5.0.17` in the checked-in files).

## Description

<!-- Please add a brief description of the changes made in this PR. If you have an ongoing or finished cmdlet design, please paste the link below. -->

Add test-only scenario coverage following the API upgrade in #30308:

- Record endpoint-role validation, cross-tenant allow-list lifecycle and invalid jobs, scheduling/partial updates, agentless connections, and description/tag updates.
- Run public and private S3 transfers through actual `Succeeded` job runs, with run-owned resource setup and cleanup.
- Exercise cmdlet serialization/deserialization and all four reconcile parameter sets through explicitly tagged offline request contracts.
- Compare JSON request bodies during new-scenario playback, including regressions for bodyless requests, equivalent JSON, and changed bodies.

The recordings contain 191 freshly recorded, sanitized HTTP exchanges. Unrelated legacy recordings and environment fields are preserved. Service-backed assertions reflect current behavior: Azure SMB Source succeeds in eastus, weekly NFS scheduling uses `None`, and tag removal is tested by replacement. MD5/synchronization and unsupported service combinations remain explicitly offline contracts, not claimed live coverage.

No production cmdlets, generated SDK, API version, module version, changelog, or help-source changes are included.

## Description

This PR adds Bicep version pinning support to Azure PowerShell's `Az.Resources` module, so Bicep deployment cmdlets can resolve, download, and cache a specific Bicep CLI version per project instead of always relying on whatever `bicep` happens to be on PATH.

### How version resolution works
1. **Config resolution (`BicepConfigResolver`)**: When a Bicep project has a `bicepconfig.json`, we look for a `bicep.version` constraint in it. If the config has an `extends` key, we walk up the chain of base config files (following each `extends` path in turn, with cycle/depth protection) until we find the effective `bicep.version` constraint - the nearest (leaf-most) config that defines one wins over any base config.
2. **Constraint parsing (`BicepVersionConstraint`)**: The constraint can be an exact version (e.g. `0.45.15`) or a range (e.g. `>=0.26.0, <0.30.0`, max 2 comparators). Malformed constraints throw a clear error naming the bad value and the config file path.
3. **PATH vs. managed install**: If a `bicep.version` constraint is present, we first check whether the `bicep` found on PATH already satisfies it (`PathExecutableSatisfiesConstraint`) - if so, we use PATH as before (no download). If PATH is missing, unparsable, or doesn't satisfy the constraint, we fall through to our managed, version-specific install cache instead of failing. If a project has **no** `bicep.version` constraint at all, behavior is unchanged: we use PATH.
4. **Caching (`BicepInstaller`)**: Managed installs are cached per-version under `~\.Azure\bin\bicep-{version}\`. Before any network call, we check whether an already-cached version satisfies the constraint and reuse it immediately. Only when no cached version satisfies the constraint do we call the Bicep release API (`GetAvailableReleaseTags`) to list real released versions and download the **highest** version that satisfies the constraint.
5. **Per-invocation caching (`BicepUtility`)**: the resolved executable path/version is now cached on the instance so a single cmdlet call that needs the Bicep path multiple times doesn't redo the PATH-check/config-lookup/install-resolution each time.

### New cmdlets
- `Get-AzBicepVersion` - lists all Bicep versions currently in the managed cache.
- `Install-AzBicep [-Version <v>]` - downloads and caches a specific version, or the latest release if `-Version` is omitted.
- `Uninstall-AzBicep [-PassThru]` - removes the **entire** managed cache (all versions), so a user can cleanly re-install afterward. Returns whether anything was actually removed (bugfix: previously always returned a hardcoded `true`).

### Test coverage
- **Constraint parsing/evaluation**: unit tests for exact-version and range constraints, valid/invalid syntax, satisfiable/unsatisfiable ranges.
- **Config resolution**: unit tests for `extends`-chain walking, including cycles, absolute paths, depth limits, and leaf-wins-over-base precedence.
- **Mocked downloader tests** (`BicepDownloaderTests`): request/response parsing logic in isolation via a fake `HttpMessageHandler`.
- **Live CDN tests** (`BicepDownloaderLiveTests`): real calls against `downloads.bicep.azure.com`, tagged `LiveOnly` and excluded from the default test run (run explicitly via `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~BicepDownloaderLiveTests"` before a release/PR).
- **Cmdlet unit tests** for `Get-AzBicepVersion`, `Install-AzBicep`, `Uninstall-AzBicep`.
- **Manual end-to-end  testing** (real `New-AzResourceGroupDeployment -WhatIf` against a live test resource group, real CDN downloads, no mocks):
  - Pinned exact version via `bicepconfig.json` (first run downloads; second run reuses cache).
  - Unpinned baseline (uses whatever's on PATH / falls back to latest managed install).
  - `extends`-chain resolution: leaf config deferring to base config's version, and leaf config overriding base's version.
  - Version-range constraints: fresh download picks the highest satisfying release, cache-hit reuse, range resolved through an `extends`-chain, invalid range syntax error, and valid-but-unsatisfiable range error (lists all real available releases).

<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/honojs/node-server/releases">@​hono/node-server's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>v2.1.6</h2>
<h2>Security fixes</h2>
<p>This release includes fixes for the following security issues:</p>
<h3>Backslash in the request path is parsed as a path separator, bypassing path-based access control at a reverse proxy</h3>
<p>Affects: all requests. The raw request-target was passed to the WHATWG URL parser, which treats a backslash in the path as <code>/</code> and resolves <code>..</code> segments, so <code>/admin\secret</code> reached the application as <code>/admin/secret</code>. A reverse proxy that forwards the backslash unchanged applied its path-based rules to the original path. <a href="https://github.com/honojs/node-server/security/advisories/GHSA-jpvv-r467-5p4w">GHSA-jpvv-r467-5p4w</a></p>
<p>A request whose path contains a raw backslash is now rejected with <code>400 Bad Request</code>, for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and WebSocket upgrades. A percent-encoded backslash (<code>%5C</code>) and a backslash in the query string are still accepted.</p>
<h3>WebSocket upgrade request-target starting with <code>//</code> replaces the host in <code>c.req.url</code>, bypassing <code>Origin</code> checks</h3>
<p>Affects: <code>upgradeWebSocket</code>. The URL of an upgrade request was built by resolving the request-target against the <code>Host</code> header, so a request-target such as <code>//attacker.example/ws</code> set the host of <code>c.req.url</code> to a client-chosen value while routing still saw <code>/ws</code>. An application that compared <code>Origin</code> with the origin of <code>c.req.url</code> could be bypassed by a page on another site. <a href="https://github.com/honojs/node-server/security/advisories/GHSA-7v5p-43qr-wch5">GHSA-7v5p-43qr-wch5</a></p>
<p>The host of upgrade requests now comes from the <code>Host</code> header, as for ordinary requests.</p>
<h3>Unhandled <code>ECONNRESET</code> on the socket during an asynchronous WebSocket upgrade crashes the process</h3>
<p>Affects: <code>upgradeWebSocket</code>. While the application handled an upgrade request, the socket had no error listener. A client that reset the connection during asynchronous middleware caused an unhandled <code>'error'</code> event and terminated the process. <a href="https://github.com/honojs/node-server/security/advisories/GHSA-qv5m-9pm6-hqp3">GHSA-qv5m-9pm6-hqp3</a></p>
<p>Error and close events on the socket are now handled while the application runs, and a pending upgrade is released when the socket closes.</p>
<hr />
<p>The backslash fix also ships in <code>@hono/node-server</code> v1.19.18. Users of <code>upgradeWebSocket</code> are encouraged to upgrade to this version.</p>
<h2>v2.1.5</h2>
<h2>What's Changed</h2>
<ul>
<li>fix(listener): abort the request signal when an HTTP/2 client resets the stream by <a href="https://github.com/affanmomin"><code>@​affanmomin</code></a> in <a href="https://redirect.github.com/honojs/node-server/pull/404">honojs/node-server#404</a></li>
<li>fix(serve-static): only serve GET and HEAD requests by <a href="https://github.com/usualoma"><code>@​usualoma</code></a> in <a href="https://redirect.github.com/honojs/node-server/pull/405">honojs/node-server#405</a></li>
</ul>
<h2>New Contributors</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/affanmomin"><code>@​affanmomin</code></a> made their first contribution in <a href="https://redirect.github.com/honojs/node-server/pull/404">honojs/node-server#404</a></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Full Changelog</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.4...v2.1.5">https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.4...v2.1.5</a></p>

<p><strong>Full Changelog</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.3...v2.1.4">https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.3...v2.1.4</a></p>
<h2>v2.1.3</h2>
<h2>Security fixes</h2>
<h3><code>serveStatic</code> decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths</h3>
<p>Affects: <code>@hono/node-server/serve-static</code>. Fixes <code>serveStatic</code> decoding an already-decoded path, where a crafted request could be routed as one path and served as another, skipping middleware mounted on a static prefix. GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f</p>

## Description

<!-- Please add a brief description of the changes made in this PR. If you have an ongoing or finished cmdlet design, please paste the link below. -->

Expanded Az.Storage management capabilities through API version 2026-09-01.

- Added service-specific Shared Key authorization controls, cross-tenant delegation SAS (shared access signature) controls, and user-bound delegation SAS enforcement to `New-AzStorageAccount` and `Set-AzStorageAccount`.
- Added Blob Access Point enablement and Turbo Tier settings to `New-AzStorageAccount` and `Set-AzStorageAccount`.
- Added `PublishIpv6Endpoint` to `New-AzStorageAccount` and `Set-AzStorageAccount` to enable or disable IPv6 endpoint publishing, and exposed the publishing preference on Storage account output.
- Added commands to manage context caches and their containers, including managed identities and name availability.
- Added commands to manage advanced platform metrics rules.
- Added commands to manage Blob Access Point configurations and test proposed or existing connections.
- Added Blob Access Point attachment parameters to `New-AzRmStorageContainer` and attachment details to management-plane container output.
- Added file-share guardrail limits and network security perimeter service tags to management output.


### Validation

- Scoped Storage build: **Passed**.
  ```powershell
  .\tools\BuildScripts\BuildModules.ps1 -RepoRoot $PWD.Path -Configuration Debug -TargetModule Storage
  ```
  
- Recorded scenarios cover account authorization policies, SAS enforcement, Turbo Tier, IPv6 endpoint publishing, container attachments, context caches, advanced platform metrics, network security perimeter operations, file-service usage, and the Blob Access Point lifecycle.

- Storage-scoped breaking-change, signature, help, and UX analyzers, followed by the final issue checker: **Passed**.

## Description

<!-- Please add a brief description of the changes made in this PR. If you have an ongoing or finished cmdlet design, please paste the link below. -->

Adds Flow VM (FlexProfile) support to Az.Compute, including preferred-size configuration, VM creation and updates, profile-preserving VM output, documentation, and recorded test coverage.

This is a standalone feature PR targeting `main`. Its complete implementation, changelog, help updates, and tests are included in this branch.

The test coverage includes the preferred-size lifecycle, fixed-size conversion, invalid-input handling, unsupported placement combinations, serialization, and preservation of VM profiles.

### Changes

- Add `PreferredVMSize` support to `New-AzVMConfig`, `New-AzVM`, and `Update-AzVM`, expose FlexProfile in VM output, and preserve preferred/actual size profiles across the affected operations.

- Correct null-object assertions and expected service/SDK errors.
- Supply deterministic DNS labels for reliable playback.
- Add start/readback after changing the preferred size while deallocated.
- Isolate nine placement/input validation cases from the lifecycle test.
- Complete the managed-disk, image, OS and network configuration for the zero-instance Flexible VMSS prerequisite.
- Check capacity-reservation association rejection with a real empty group instead of depending on allocating reservation capacity.
- Correct the help example's unsupported image alias.
- Add all ten complete recordings from feature-enabled East Asia.

### Validation

Historical local validation was performed on October 23, 2026. The repository workflow is documented in `.github/instructions/compute-test-debugging.instructions.md` and `documentation/testing-docs/using-azure-test-framework.md`.

**Current main integration, October 26:** Commit `5396af94401590069e576d978e04a2bdfbbec6c8` incorporates main `e9feb37fa42fec0d878f3e544a5b00ce8fa256df` and preserves both Compute changelog entries. GitHub now reports the PR is conflict-free. **CI status, October 26:** Both builds, all Linux/macOS/Windows test jobs, Windows PowerShell analysis, and security-tools passed. The PowerShell Core Analyze job failed while downloading PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 from PowerShell Gallery ([run 366277](https://dev.azure.com/azclitools/5147fa83-336e-44ef-bbe0-c86b8ae86cbb/_build/results?buildId=366277&view=logs)). An attempted failed-job-only retry was denied by Azure DevOps permissions, so an authorized pipeline maintainer must retry Analyze. No source fix or additional recording was made for this download failure. Required CI is not fully green yet.

#### Latest local validation

The published merge commit has tree `a35f30a5482eaef7736ea1672360446259548255`, exactly matching the integration validated before publication.

- Required module preparation/build: passed.
- Compute test-assembly rebuild: passed, zero errors. Four existing dependency-advisory warnings were reported.
- **62 cases executed, 62 passed, zero failed, zero skipped:** all ten recorded PowerShell scenarios plus all 52 recording-independent cases added by this PR.
- The earlier fresh-checkout module-loading failures were resolved by preparing the complete module artifacts. No FlexProfile source change or new recording was needed for that setup issue.
- No live Azure resources were created during the October 26 Playback run.

Commands executed:

```powershell
& (Join-Path $repo 'tools\BuildScripts\BuildModules.ps1') -RepoRoot $repo -Configuration Debug `
    -TargetModule @('Compute', 'Network', 'KeyVault', 'ManagedServiceIdentity')

dotnet build $project --no-restore --configuration Debug --framework net8.0

dotnet test $project --no-build --no-restore --configuration Debug --framework net8.0 `
    --filter $selection.filter --logger 'trx;LogFileName=CombinedFlexProfile.Playback.trx' `
    --logger 'console;verbosity=normal' --results-directory $run
```

`$selection.filter` is an exact-name OR filter for all 29 added Fact/Theory methods, yielding 62 cases. The recorded result is `artifacts\CombinedFlexProfileValidation\20261026-131306-module-prepared\CombinedFlexProfile.Playback.trx` in the isolated validation checkout. The build used the previously working package-feed proxy configuration without changing repository configuration.

#### Historical live recording generation, October 23

All ten scenarios also have passing live recordings. These were accumulated across corrected recording runs, not a single final ten-case live invocation. The historical recording and replay commands/results follow.

The commands used were:

```powershell
$solution = Join-Path $repo 'src\Compute\Compute.sln'
$project = Join-Path $repo 'src\Compute\Compute.Test\Compute.Test.csproj'
$prefix = 'Microsoft.Azure.Commands.Compute.Test.ScenarioTests.VirtualMachineTests.'

dotnet build $solution --no-restore --configuration Debug

dotnet test $project --no-build --no-restore --configuration Debug --framework net8.0 `
    --filter $filter --logger 'trx;LogFileName=FlexProfile.Record.trx' `
    --logger 'console;verbosity=normal' --results-directory $run

dotnet test $project --no-build --no-restore --configuration Debug --framework net8.0 `
    --filter ('FullyQualifiedName~' + $prefix + 'TestFlexProfile') `
    --logger 'trx;LogFileName=FlexProfile.Playback.trx' `
    --logger 'console;verbosity=normal' --results-directory $run
```

`$repo` was the local Azure PowerShell checkout. TestFx was explicitly set to Record or Playback before the corresponding invocation.

| Execution | Filter | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Build | Compute solution, Debug | Passed, zero errors. Final build reported five warnings, including dependency advisories and a recovered file-copy retry |
| Initial isolated Record | Prefix filter for `TestFlexProfile` | 10 executed, 6 passed, 4 failed. Failures were corrected and re-recorded below |
| Corrected Record | Exact-name OR filter for `TestFlexProfileHostGroupValidation`, `TestFlexProfileNullPreferredSizeValidation`, `TestFlexProfileVmssValidation`, `TestFlexProfileCapacityReservationValidation` | 4 executed, 4 passed |
| Final DNS-corrected Record | Exact-name OR filter for `TestFlexProfile`, `TestFlexProfileHostGroupValidation`, `TestFlexProfileNullPreferredSizeValidation` | 3 executed, 3 passed |
| Final Playback | Prefix filter for `TestFlexProfile` | 10 executed, 10 passed, zero failed or skipped |

For the subset invocations, `$filter` was `($remaining | ForEach-Object { 'FullyQualifiedName=' + $prefix + $_ }) -join '|'`, using the method lists above. The `$run` directories under `artifacts\FlexProfileValidation` were `20261023-133255-isolated`, `20261023-150922-record-playback`, and `20261023-152423-dns-record-playback`.

All ten scenarios have passing live recordings across the corrected runs. This does not claim a single final ten-case live invocation. Final Playback evidence is `20261023-152423-dns-record-playback\FlexProfile.Playback.trx`. No test resource groups remained after cleanup.

### Coverage limits

- Capacity-reservation coverage validates rejection of a real **empty group**, not populated reservations or capacity fulfillment.
- VMSS coverage uses a real **zero-instance Flexible scale set**, not scale-out.
- Null-preference simple creation is rejected by SDK validation before a VM PUT. Network prerequisites are still created and cleaned up.
- Observed updates used HTTP PUT, not PATCH.
- The full Az.Compute suite was not run. The October 26 local integration run added coverage of 52 recording-independent cases, all of which passed. No all-region/cloud, alternative-size fulfillment, guest-workload, billing or performance validation is claimed.

The complete PR includes the implementation's public cmdlet additions, help and changelog changes together with the recorded tests. The latest test/help commit does not adjust module versions or add further public cmdlet APIs.

Flow VMs specify a preferred size while allowing Azure to deploy a compatible alternative. These changes expose FlexProfile and preserve it across read-modify-write operations.

- **Creation:** Add `-PreferredVMSize` to `New-AzVMConfig` and simple `New-AzVM`. Enforce size exclusivity, omit fixed size from FlexProfile requests, and retain CPU customization settings.
- **Updates and output:** Expose `FlexProfile` on VM objects. Let `Update-AzVM -PreferredVMSize` override fixed size without mutating the input object; preserve both profiles on ordinary round trips.
- **Encryption:** Forward FlexProfile through disk-encryption paths that rebuild VM requests.
- **Coverage and documentation:** Add binding, serialization, lifecycle, placement, encryption, and AEM regressions; update help, examples, and changelogs.

```powershell
$config = New-AzVMConfig -VMName "vm1" -PreferredVMSize "Standard_D4s_v5"

Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName "rg1" -Name "vm1" |
    Update-AzVM -PreferredVMSize "Standard_D8s_v5"
```

To return to a fixed size, clear `$vm.FlexProfile`, set `$vm.HardwareProfile.VmSize`, and update without `-PreferredVMSize`. Preview usage requires `Microsoft.Compute/FlexProfileEnabled` registration and a supported region.

## Verification Checklist
- [ ] Confirm parameter metadata, size exclusivity, and positional compatibility.
- [ ] Confirm SDK model mapping, request forwarding, and input immutability.
- [ ] Verify help syntax ordering, parameter placement, examples, and changelog entries.
- [ ] Review coverage for conversion, opt-out, rejected inputs, CPU preservation, NoWait, encryption, and AEM.
- [ ] Confirm scenario entry points are wired as CheckIn tests and assertions verify persisted state.

## Description

Updates Az.PlanetaryComputer to the Microsoft.Orbital management API version **2026-10-01**.

- Pins AutoRest to the immutable public specification commit `9ecfd7c772db95534126fb62a2e983d9145bbd57`.
- Adds GeoCatalog private-link discovery and private-endpoint connection get/list, create, update and remove cmdlets.
- Adds Premium configuration, public network access, and read-only lifecycle properties while preserving the existing GeoCatalog command names and module version.
- Regenerates the canonical generated project, parent exports, reference help and examples.
- Adds one real, sanitized read-only integration recording covering private-link discovery and connection list/get.

Related drafts:
- Public API specification: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/47502
- Azure CLI extension: https://github.com/Azure/azure-cli-extensions/pull/10503

### Validation

- AutoRest generation and standalone module build succeeded.
- Both the canonical generated project and parent module build succeeded with zero warnings and zero errors.
- Imported the packaged parent module and verified all nine exported commands.
- Focused Pester scenario passed live against regional ARM in `eastus2euap`, then offline through the standard generated playback runner: **1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Recording contains three successful GET interactions, all using `2026-10-01`; authorization, identifiers and account information are sanitized.
- Six deliberate mutations of recording copies were detected: API version, private-link group, required member, required DNS zone, connection identity and approval status. Restoring the healthy recording passed.
- PowerShell parser checks and staged whitespace checks passed.
- No live resources were created, changed or deleted for this PowerShell validation.

To reproduce the focused playback after building the two projects:

```powershell
dotnet build generated/PlanetaryComputer/PlanetaryComputer.Autorest/Az.PlanetaryComputer.csproj
dotnet build src/PlanetaryComputer/PlanetaryComputer/PlanetaryComputer.csproj
pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File artifacts/Debug/Az.PlanetaryComputer/PlanetaryComputer.Autorest/test-module.ps1 -Playback -TestName Get-AzPlanetaryComputerGeoCatalogPrivateLink
```

### Draft / remaining work

- Cmdlet design review is required for the added public commands; no approval is claimed.
- The specification PR is still open; this draft deliberately pins its available immutable commit.
- New PowerShell write-operation/lifecycle recordings and a refresh of the legacy GeoCatalog recordings remain pending. The legacy tapes still target `2026-04-15`; no full-suite pass is claimed, and existing tests were not skipped or relabeled.
- Global ARM did not expose this version during validation. Live PowerShell requests used a process-scoped regional environment; no regional endpoint is hardcoded in the generated module.
- Private DNS and data-plane connectivity were not tested.
