## Summary
- Update Az.PrivateTrafficManager to the public 2026-10-01-preview API, pinned to Azure REST API specs commit 1e7fff538a7e9d7ca6127b349295c467601362a0.
- Regenerate the module while preserving its GUID and add four ProfileProbingGateway association commands (24 total exports).
- Support CustomTopologyMapMode Enabled/Disabled, VNet routing and endpoint assignments, updated health-policy probe fields, and restricted topology-map PATCH properties.
- Refresh examples, changelogs, generated documentation and packaged parent help.
- Add offline model/HTTP contract tests, an isolated live validation runner, and sanitized October recording playback.

## Validation
- Scoped module build and built-module import succeeded.
- 44 focused offline Pester tests passed, with zero failures or skips.
- Eight live scenarios passed against 2026-10-01-preview: profile PATCH, gateway association CRUD and parent identity binding, health-policy field preservation, weighted endpoints, VNet assignments/fallback, topology/site CRUD and PATCH, delete postconditions, and verified cleanup.
- All eight scenarios passed credential-free playback using 92 sanitized HTTP exchanges.
- Parent Markdown/MAML help validated for all 24 commands.
- Scoped dependency/signature/help/UX/check-error analysis passed with no blocking errors; nonblocking generator signature/shared-assembly warnings remain.
- Error-level PSScriptAnalyzer and git diff --check passed.
- All four temporary validation groups were confirmed deleted. The existing probing gateway was referenced only, not modified.

## Known Service Issue and Coverage Gaps
- Resource-group bulk deletion currently dispatches the February API and cannot delete VNet-routing profiles. The live runner explicitly deletes owned PTM resources through October cmdlets before deleting its group.
- Advanced-profile topology binding/mode transitions, duplicate VNet/fallback rejection, Priority/AAAA/CNAME variants, and DNS/probing data-plane behavior are not yet covered by live validation.
- The October playback runner is invoked explicitly; it is not yet integrated into the legacy test-module.ps1 harness.
- Existing February recordings and skipped legacy scenarios remain unchanged.

## Base Branch
Targets private-msi/Az.PrivateTrafficManager, the integration branch used by the original onboarding PR #29729. This keeps the PR limited to the two October implementation/validation commits and avoids inherited unrelated changes in a comparison against main.

## Description

Adds Azure-to-Azure Confidential VM (CVM) PowerShell support using Site Recovery API version `2026-11-01`.

Related public Swagger PR: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/46144

### Changes

- Pin the Site Recovery SDK README to public Swagger commit `e30a8941fbdc2e5ebc90ffd912710e9175db1c07` (merge commit of Swagger PR #46144) instead of a private spec fork. Regenerate from the latest public PR contract, retaining the dual-stack examples and response-only `ipVersion` correction.
- Update the in-repository generated SDK to API `2026-11-01`, including confidential disk encryption models. Generated IPv6 and recovery-network auto-sync properties are included because they are part of the same API contract.
- Add per-disk replica/target confidential DES parameters and forward them through existing A2A enable, add-disk, and individual reprotect paths.
- Add recovery confidential data disk encryption identity inputs for enable, update, and individual reprotect. Disk updates support the target confidential DES, not changing the replica confidential DES.
- Expose recovery identity and per-disk confidential DES values in PowerShell protected-item output.
- Add CVM unit/scenario coverage and help for disk configuration, enable, add disk, update, individual reprotect, and readback.

This does not implement A2A recovery-plan reprotect. It does not change the shared vault SDK API version or publish a standalone .NET SDK package.

## Description

New autorest-generated module **Az.Commvault** (`0.1.0`) for the Azure Native ISV service Liftr-Commvault, generated from the **stable** Commvault.ContentStore API `2026-09-30` (azure-rest-api-specs `specification/liftrcommvault`, tag `package-2026-09-30`, pinned to commit `e91f0b95c03a435a7d745e8c70930aadce552d39`).

**Cmdlets (34):** cloud accounts (`New/Get/Update/Remove-AzCommvaultCloudAccount`), plans, storages, protection groups, role mapping, protected items, plus action cmdlets (`Backup-`, `Restore-`, `Resume-`/`Stop-…ProtectionGroupBackup`, `Enable-`/`Disable-AzCommvaultStorageComplianceLock`, `Sync-AzCommvaultStorage`, `Get-AzCommvaultProtectedItemRestorePoint`/`ProtectedItemCount`, `Initialize-AzCommvaultSaaS`, `Connect-AzCommvaultCloudAccountSaaS`, `Get-AzCommvaultCloudAccountLatestLinkedSaaS`).

**Design review:** no cmdlet design review issue was filed for this module. The cmdlets are generated by autorest.powershell; the names that differ from the plain Get/New/Update/Remove pattern come from the operation names in the spec and are documented with a comment per directive in `Commvault.Autorest/README.md` (for example `Sync-AzCommvaultStorage` for the storage refresh action and `-StorageClassType` for the `class` property, which would otherwise end in a plural). Happy to open a design review if the team would like one.

**Validation done locally** (same steps as the `powershell-core` pipeline): Build, Analyze (static analysis exits 0; the Signature check reports warnings only, ConfirmImpact on the `Get-` list cmdlets, as for Az.Informatica) and Test. All 56 documented examples were also executed against a local mock ARM server generated from the swagger and its examples, with request bodies validated against the schema.

**Tests:** the generated test stubs are skipped (`-skip`). Creating a cloud account needs a real Commvault SaaS activation through the Azure Marketplace, so live recordings are not possible yet.

**Known service-side limitations** (being raised with the Commvault RP team, not caused by the module): protection group and protected item operations require a user-context token that Azure PowerShell cannot obtain yet, and `Connect-AzCommvaultCloudAccountSaaS` / `Get-AzCommvaultCloudAccountLatestLinkedSaaS` call actions that are declared in the spec but not yet implemented by the service.
